cases.name: 0^docs from a top-level row is the named root (≡ ^docs)
cases.notes: Scope depth is syntactic (GRAMMAR §4): the root is 0, a top-level row 1. `N^name` desugars in the parser to the `outer` reference reaching scope N, here `^docs`.
cases.query: id, n: size(0^docs), same: 0^docs is ^docs from docs

cases.name: 0^$it from a top-level row is the root object (≡ ^$it)
cases.query: id, k: 0^$it.k, same: 0^$it is ^$it from docs

cases.name: 0^k in a top-level where
cases.query: id values from docs where n == 0^k

cases.name: two deep: 0^docs is the root and 1^path the top-level row
cases.notes: Inside a select-position block under a top-level row the body is depth 2, so `1^path` is `^path` and `0^docs` is `^^docs`.
cases.query: id, t: tasks collect { text, doc: 1^path, same: 1^path is ^path, all: size(0^docs) } from docs

cases.name: three deep: every enclosing scope by number
cases.notes: The leaf block's body is depth 3: `2^v` is the mid row, `1^v` the top row, `0^rows` the named root, `0^$it` the root object.
cases.query: m: mid collect { l: leaf collect { own: v, one: 2^v, two: 1^v, n: size(0^rows), root: 0^$it.rows[0].v } } from rows

cases.name: the caret form and the numbered form are one tree
cases.query: m: mid collect { l: leaf collect { a: 2^v is ^v, b: 1^v is ^^v, c: 0^rows is ^^^rows } } from rows

cases.name: 0^docs as a where receiver
cases.query: id values from docs where 0^docs exists { where id == ^ref && id != ^id }

cases.name: 0^$it.docs as a select receiver, entries(0^$it) as a source
cases.query: id, others: 0^$it.docs collect { id values where id != ^id }, roots: entries(0^$it) collect { $key values } from docs

cases.name: composes with brackets: 0^docs[0] and x[p == 0^flag]
cases.query: id, head: 0^docs[0].id, second: 0^$it.docs[1].id, open: tasks[done == 0^flag].text from docs

cases.name: as a lift target: 1^open: text binds into the top-level row
cases.notes: A where-position collect's body is depth 2; `1^open:` is the lift `^open:` into the depth-1 row.
cases.query: id, open from docs where tasks collect { 1^open: text where !done }

cases.name: inside a follow destination block: the receiver and the frontier row by number
cases.notes: The destination's receiver is read in the frontier row's scope (depth 1), so `0^people` is `^people`; its body is depth 2, so `1^id` is `^id`, the frontier row.
cases.query: name values from people where id == 1 follow 0^people collect { where manager == 1^id } order by $ordinal

cases.name: inside follow where: 1^id is the frontier row, 0^k the root
cases.notes: A follow `where` reads the successor's scope hung off the frontier row (SEMANTICS §20), depth 2 under a top-level walk: `1^id` is `^id`, `0^k` is `^^k`.
cases.query: id values from chain where id == 1 follow next { where prev == 1^id && 0^k == 2 } order by $ordinal

cases.name: inside follow where: a root comparison that fails prunes every successor
cases.query: id values from chain where id == 1 follow next { where prev == 1^id && 0^k == 3 }

cases.name: inside a bound: 1^n in a block's limit is the enclosing row
cases.notes: A block's bound is read in the row-less scope inside the block (SEMANTICS §18), the block's own depth (2 here), so `1^n` is `^n`.
cases.query: name, top: scores collect { $it values limit 1^n } from r

cases.name: N must be below the current depth: 1^ at depth 1
cases.query: id from docs where 1^k == 2

includes: scope 1 does not enclose this block

cases.name: N must be below the current depth: 2^ at depth 2
cases.query: id, t: tasks collect { x: 2^text } from docs

includes: scope 2 does not enclose this block

cases.name: the top-level source is read at the root: 0^ has nothing to reach
cases.query: id from 0^docs

includes: scope 0 does not enclose this block

cases.name: a top-level bound is read at the root: limit 0^n is the same error
cases.query: id from docs limit 0^n

includes: scope 0 does not enclose this block

cases.name: the integer and the caret must touch: `1 ^k` is not a scope reference
cases.query: id from docs where 1 ^k == 2

cases.name: only an unsigned integer literal: `1.0^k` is not a scope reference
cases.query: id from docs where 1.0^k == 2

cases.name: at a select item's head N^ is a lift, with the lift's own rules
cases.query: 0^name from docs

cases.name: AST: 1^$path inside a nested block parses to outer { levels: 1 }
cases.query: docs collect { t: tasks collect { p: 1^$path } }

cases.name: AST: 0^k at depth 1 is outer { levels: 1 } in select and where alike
cases.query: select k: 0^k from docs where 0^k == 2

cases.name: AST: 1^open: in a where-position collect is the lift { lift: 1 }
cases.query: docs collect { open where tasks collect { 1^open: text } }
